archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose production now runs through improvised scrambles off broken dropbacks rather than designed runs, with a passing game that has settled into the league's middle tier since his rookie year.

report.headline: His legs are carrying a passing game still stuck below his rookie level
report.take:
Daniels arrived as one of the most complete young quarterbacks in the league. In 2024 he ranked 9th in EPA per play at 0.204, completed 69% of his passes and ran for 891 yards. The rushing has held up. The passing has not. Over seven games in 2025 he fell to 0.029 EPA per play with a -2.7 CPOE. Three games into 2026 he sits at 0.021 per dropback, 24th of 43, with 6.04 yards per attempt, 36th. That makes about ten straight games of middling passing, which is long enough to stop calling it a blip.

What keeps him a top-six fantasy quarterback at 21.6 PPR a game is scrambling, not scheme. Of his 203 rushing yards, 201 came on 16 scrambles, and those produced 10 first downs at 1.078 EPA apiece. He takes off on 16% of his dropbacks. His four designed runs gained 3 yards combined, and half of them were stuffed. Washington isn't building the run game around him; he is creating it when the pocket breaks down. The 32.3-point game against the Giants is the clearest example: 103 rushing yards and two scores on the same day his passing EPA was -2.4 and he was sacked five times.

The passing profile splits sharply by depth. Between 10 and 19 yards he has been excellent: 12 of 17, 0.781 EPA per throw, a 22.5 CPOE. Deep, he is 2 of 12. His 10 throws behind the line cost 0.843 EPA each, even with 8 of them completed, so the screen game is losing yards. On third down the offense keeps facing 8.9 yards to go and converts 30.4%. The pressure numbers look clean this year (14.3% pressured, 9.1% pressure-to-sack), but they rest on partial charting; the Giants game, with its five sacks, has none. His career pressure-to-sack rates of 41% and 44% ranked near the bottom of the league. Holding the ball to buy scramble lanes is part of who he is. So far the scrambles more than pay for the 7.3% sack rate, but the cost is real.

The zero interceptions also deserve caution. He threw 9 as a rookie, and a no-pick start over 76 attempts is more luck than a new skill. With Stefon Diggs out and Jaylin Lane on injured reserve, the passing ceiling narrows further. His weekly floor will keep coming from his legs.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: His 16 scrambles produced 201 yards, 10 first downs and more than a full point of EPA each. This is the engine of both his real value and his fantasy value. It holds up across seasons: he ranked 2nd in rushing yards as a rookie and ranks 2nd again now. The efficiency per scramble will cool, but the volume is part of how he plays.

strengths.title: Accurate in the intermediate window
strengths.body: On throws of 10-19 air yards he has completed 70.6% at 0.781 EPA, well above expectation. This is the part of his passing that still looks like 2024. Seventeen attempts is a small sample, so expect the CPOE to come down. The underlying accuracy at this depth is the best case for a passing rebound.

strengths.title: Clean on the ball so far
strengths.body: He has no interceptions and no lost fumbles through three games, and charting shows just one turnover-worthy fumble. Some of this is real: he was 17th in interceptions in 2025. But he threw 9 picks as a rookie, so a few are coming.

concerns.title: Passing has plateaued since his rookie year
concerns.body: His 0.021 EPA per dropback and 6.04 yards per attempt match his 2025 level, not the 0.204 EPA of his rookie season. Two seasons pointing the same way make this the current baseline rather than noise. The receiver injuries give no reason to expect a quick fix.

concerns.title: The deep ball has disappeared
concerns.body: He has two completions on 12 throws of 20+ air yards, 17 points below expected. The 0.078 EPA on those throws suggests something positive happened beyond the catches, since only two connected. Without completions down the field, defenses can squeeze everything underneath.

concerns.title: Sacks are the price of extending
concerns.body: A 7.3% sack rate ranks 30th, and the Giants got him five times. His career pressure-to-sack rates were bottom-ten in both prior seasons. That is a trait tied to the scrambling rather than a new flaw, but it drives the drive-killing third-and-longs.

trend.note: His passing EPA has dropped each game: 3.9, then 0.2 in a 55%-snap outing, then -2.4. His rushing has climbed from 31 to 69 to 103 yards. The result is fantasy swings from 14.7 to 32.3 that depend almost entirely on his legs.

nextGame.headline: Big road underdog against a defense that erases explosive plays
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's defense ranks 4th in EPA and 1st in preventing explosive passes and explosive runs. It is 6th against deep throws, which is exactly where Daniels is already failing. The soft spot is underneath: SF ranks 21st on short passes and lets running backs see a 25.5% target share against an 18.2% league norm. That points the passing game toward checkdowns and the intermediate middle, where he has been sharp. As a 7.5-point underdog facing the league's top passing offense with his own 25th-ranked pass defense, Washington should be throwing from behind. That means more dropbacks and more chances to scramble. Quarterbacks have managed just 13.1 PPR a game against SF, 6th fewest.

Availability cuts both ways. Washington is without Diggs, who had 12 targets at 0.594 EPA each, and Lane. That leaves McLaurin, Chig Okonkwo and Antonio Williams to carry the targets. Williams looks interesting given SF's 28th rank against WR3s. On SF's side, Dre Greenlaw is suspended, Garret Wallow is out and Nick Martin is on IR, which thins the linebackers who would chase Daniels on scrambles. Starting safety Marques Sigle is also out. Nick Bosa "has a chance" to return from his calf injury. His presence would matter most for Daniels' sack problem.

keyMatchups.title: Scrambles against a thinned linebacker room
keyMatchups.body: With Greenlaw suspended and Wallow out, SF's second level is short on the players who spy and rally to a scrambling quarterback. Daniels is producing over a point of EPA per scramble. SF's top-ranked explosive-run defense will try to keep those runs short, but chain-moving scrambles don't need to be long.

keyMatchups.title: Underneath open, deep closed
keyMatchups.body: SF is 21st against short passes but 6th against deep ones and 1st at limiting explosive passes. That fits a quarterback who is efficient in the middle (0.601 EPA) and failing deep. Expect a lower-aDOT plan with plenty of back and tight-end targets.

keyMatchups.title: Trailing script forces volume
keyMatchups.body: SF's passing offense ranks 1st in EPA, and Washington's pass defense ranks 25th. Daniels should spend much of this game behind. He has been efficient when down two scores (0.479 EPA, 12 plays), which helps his volume more than Washington's chances.

nextGame.watch: Whether Bosa plays. Without him, SF's middling pass rush and depleted linebackers leave room for Daniels to extend and run. With him, the sack problem gets worse.

restOfSeason.body:
The rushing is the bankable part. He ranks 2nd in rushing yards for the second time in three seasons, and scrambles on about one in six dropbacks give him a fantasy floor most quarterbacks lack. The 9.67 yards per carry and 0.649 EPA per carry will come down as the scramble sample grows and defenses spy him more, but 40-60 rushing yards a game is a fair expectation. The passing is harder to trust. Two seasons of league-average efficiency, a nonexistent deep game and failing screens point to more of the same, especially until Diggs returns.

Expect regression in two directions. The zero interceptions should give way to a normal rate. The intermediate efficiency should cool from its current pace. The sack rate should settle somewhere in between, high but probably not five a game. If Diggs comes back healthy and the deep shots start connecting, the passing could climb toward his rookie form. Otherwise he stays a rushing-driven fantasy QB1 with a mid-pack real passing profile.
swingFactors: Diggs' hamstring and the health of the receiver room
Whether the deep ball starts connecting
Sack volume behind a line ranked 22nd in hits allowed

bets.reason: Nearly all of his rushing comes from scrambles, and a trailing script against SF adds dropbacks. SF is missing Greenlaw and Wallow at linebacker. He has topped 52 yards in two of three games.
He hasn't reached 200 passing yards this season, and Diggs is out. SF ranks 1st at preventing explosive passes and 6th on deep throws, where Daniels is 2 of 12. Trailing volume is the main risk.
He has thrown 3 TDs in 3 games and only 1 in his last two. SF allows just 1.2 TDs a game to quarterbacks (5th fewest), and his red-zone completion rate is 44.4%.

All three of his games went over. SF's top-ranked passing offense faces Washington's 25th-ranked pass defense, and SF's defense is missing Sigle, Greenlaw and possibly Bosa. SF's elite explosive-play defense keeps this a modest edge.

confidence.note: Three games and 76 attempts, with a 55%-snap game and partial pressure charting, but two prior seasons give clear context.
